Heard learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company and learned counsel for cross-objector-claimant.

M.F.A.No.100157/2017 is filed by the Insurance Company challenging on the ground of liability and quantum of compensation and MFA.CROB No.100058/2018 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation by modifying the judgment and award darted 07.10.2016 passed in MVC.No.1033/2012 by the Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T. Bailhongal ("the Tribunal" for short),
where by the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.1.10.080/- to the claimant.
3. Both the appeals are arising out of the common judgment and award of the Tribunal.
Hence, they are heard together and disposed of by this common judgment.
4. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as they are referred to in the claim petition before the Tribunal.

-4-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:9869  MFA.CROB No. 100058 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 100157 of 2017 Sri. Yallappa S/O. Basappa Tegur vs Sri. Appayya Sateri Kurabar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143236794/

The claimant had filed claim petition under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("M.V.Act" for short) claiming compensation on account of injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 18.07.2011, when the claimant was proceeding as pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA.22/ED 7493,
which was ridden by respondent No.1, rider cum owner of the motorcycle.
When the motorcycle came near the spot of accident on Itagi Cross, N.H.4, the driver of unknown Truck came from Belagavi side in a high speed and negligent manner dashed to the motorcycle.

Hence, the rider of the motorcycle succumbed to the accidental injuries and claimant sustained following injuries:
 i. Compartment of Syndrome  ii. Fracture of distal end of right Tibia.

iii. Facture of right medial mallalous.
 6.
Considering the oral an documentary evidence on record
, the Tribunal has awarded compensation in a sum of Rs.1,10,080/- to the claimant.

Being aggrieved by the same,
the insurance company has filed MFA.No.100157/20017  -5-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:9869  MFA.CROB No. 100058 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 100157 of 2017 challenging the liability and thereafter the claimant has filed cross-objection in MFA.CROB.No.100058/2018.
 7.

Learned counsel for the Insurance Company has taken a contention that the rider of motorcycle was not Sri. Yallappa S/O. Basappa Tegur vs Sri. Appayya Sateri Kurabar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143236794/
4 possessing valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the rider was himself tortfeasor.
Hence, the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and thus, the claimant being a pillion rider cannot maintain petition under Section 163A of the M.V.Act.
Hence, she prays to allow the appeal filed by the Insurance Company and dismiss the cross objection filed by the claimant.

8. Learned counsel for the claimant contended that,
the Tribunal has not considered the proper income of the claimant. The Tribunal considered income of the clamant at Rs.3,000/- per month and awarded total compensation of Rs.55,080/- towards loss of future income, hence, it has to be enhanced.
Further the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
Thus, he prayed to enhance the compensation.

After hearing both the parties, the points that would arise for Court's consideration in this appeal are as follows;
 1. Whether the insurance company has made out  sufficient grounds that as the rider of motorcycle  was not possessing valid and effective driving  licence, hence, it is not liable to pay any  compensation to the claimant?
2. Whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal  is just and reasonable or does it call for any  interference for enhancement?
Sri. Yallappa S/O. Basappa Tegur vs Sri. Appayya Sateri Kurabar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143236794/
The insurance company has taken contention that the rider of motorcycle was not possessing valid and effective driving licence and therefore the claimant is not entitled any compensation.

In order to establish this aspect,
the Insurance Company has not examined any witness before the Tribunal and none of the documents were marked in evidence.
On the contrary the claimant relied upon Exs.P.1 to P.31 and oral evidence of PWs.1 & 2.

The contents of Ex.P.1-complaint, Ex.P.2-FIR, Ex.P.3-Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5- Wound Certificate, Ex.P.6-Charge sheet and Ex.P.7- Discharge card, clearly establish that the Investigating Officer filed charge sheet against the driver of lorry.

From the perusal of Ex.P.5-Wound Certificate,
Ex.P.7-Discharge Card, the claimant sustained injuries.

i.e.,
Compartment of Syndrome, Fracture of distal end of right Tibia and Fracture of right medial mallalous.

12. The contents of charge sheet are not challenged by the Insurance Company and contents of charge sheet shows that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the lorry.

Thus, it is just and necessary to analyze Section 163A of the M.V.Act.
 "163A.
Special provisions as to payment of  compensation on structured formula basis.

 compensation, as indicated in the Second Schedule, to the  legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.

Explanation.--For the purposes of this sub-section,
 "permanent disability" shall have the same meaning and  extent as in the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of  1923).

(2) In any claim for compensation under sub-  section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or  establish that the death or permanent disablement in  respect of which the claim has been made was due to any  wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the  vehicle or vehicles concerned or of any other person.

 from time to time amend the Second Schedule."

13. From the perusal of the aforesaid proposition,
Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, provided for payment of compensation on structured formula basis by mandating that the owner of a motor vehicle or the authorized insurer would be liable to pay compensation, as indicated in the second schedule in the case of death or permanent disability due to accident arising out of the use of the motorcycle, to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be in a claim made under sub Section (1) of Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.

In order to prove a claim of this nature, the claimant need not be required to plead or establish that the death or permanent Sri. Yallappa S/O. Basappa Tegur vs Sri. Appayya Sateri Kurabar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143236794/
7 disablement in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or negligent or default of the owner of the vehicle concerned.
14. The Hon'ble apex Court in the case of Chandrakanth Tiwari Vs.
New India Assurance Company Limited

and another1 has held as follows:
1  (2020) 5 SCR 868  -9-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:9869  MFA.CROB No. 100058 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 100157 of 2017  HELD:
The claimant need not plead or establish that the  death in respect of which the claim was made, was due to  any negligence or default of the owner of the vehicle or of  any other person.
(emphasis supplied).

It is not relevant  that the person insured must be the driver of the vehicle  but may well have been riding with somebody else driving a  vehicle which resulted in the death of the person driving the  vehicle.

The High Court is clearly wrong in stating that it  was necessary under Section 163-A to prove that somebody  else was driving the vehicle rashly and negligently, as a  result of which, the death of the victim would take place.
 15.

A perusal of this provision would show that the claimant need not plead or establish that the injuries in respect of which the claim was made was due to any negligence or default of the rider or owner of the vehicle.
In this view of the matter, it is not relevant that the person insured must be the driver of the vehicle.

16. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case and ratio laid down in the decision cited supra, the insurance Sri. Yallappa S/O. Basappa Tegur vs Sri. Appayya Sateri Kurabar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143236794/
8 company is liable to pay compensation to the claimant.

sentences.text: 17. Insofar as quantum of the compensation is concerned, the learned counsel for the claimant contended that, the Tribunal has awarded a meager compensation under the head of loss of future income, considering the monthly income of the claimants at Rs.3,000/-.

In fact, the  - 10 -  NC: 2024:KHC-D:9869  MFA.CROB No. 100058 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 100157 of 2017 Tribunal ought to have considered Rs.40,000/- per annum,
as per Schedule-II of the M.V.Act.
The doctor has assessed disability at 30% to the right lower limb as per disability certificate Ex.P.29.
But the Tribunal without assigning proper reasons considered the permanent disability at 9%, hence the disability has to be taken at 10%.

If the income of the claimant at Rs.40,000/- per annum is taken into consideration, considering '17' multiplier and 10%
permanent physical disability, loss of future income would work out to Rs.68,000/- (Rs.40,000/- X 17 X 10/100).

18. The Tribunal considering nature of injuries awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards pain and suffering which is reasonable and hence no interference is called for in this regard.
 19.

So far as the medical expenses is concerned, the Tribunal has granted a sum of Rs.50,000/-, where the Sri. Yallappa S/O. Basappa Tegur vs Sri. Appayya Sateri Kurabar on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143236794/
9 deceased or injured is not having any income, though the II Schedule of the M.V.Act., presumes medical expenses at Rs.15,000/-.

United India Insurance Company Limited
- 11 -  NC: 2024:KHC-D:9869  MFA.CROB No. 100058 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 100157 of 2017 and another2 has held at paragraph Nos.13 and 14

has held as under:
 "13. What would be the genuine and reasonable  expenditure likely to be incurred by the appellant  towards her future treatment is not borne out from  the records.
It would require serious consideration for  the purpose of award of damages.

When a person  becomes completely incapable to do any work and  virtually has no enjoyment for life, the same form  relevant factors and, thus, requires consideration for  the purpose of determining a fair and reasonable  amount of compensation.
 14.
It has not been disputed that future  treatment for the appellant would be necessary.
If  future treatment is necessary, some provision should  be made therefor.
It absence of any clear-cut  estimate, we are inclined to award a further sum of  Rs.75,000/- under the said head.
She may require  another operation.
She may require tobe provided  with an artificial limb.
We, direct accordingly."

20. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Sapna's case (supra)
considering the nature of injuries and treatment required to the claimant, awarded a sum of Rs.75,000/- under the head of medical expense.
Hence, in the instant case, the Tribunal is right in awarding a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards medical expenses.
